userStories.notes: Seed story completed. Generated 11 pipeline-focused stories (US-44-002 through US-44-012) based on comprehensive codebase analysis. Key themes: state validation consistency, checkpoint integrity, error context, config validation, code deduplication, cross-stage data flow testing, and match serialization consistency.

userStories.title: Add pipeline-level config validation at startup before any stage runs
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline.__init__ or run() calls a new _validate_config() method before iterating stages
_validate_config() checks that config.cache.cache_dir path is writable (or can be created)
_validate_config() checks that the embedding provider is configured when matching stages are enabled
_validate_config() returns a list of validation errors; pipeline logs them and returns False if critical errors exist
Tests verify that an invalid config (e.g., non-writable cache dir) causes pipeline to fail fast with a descriptive error
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (reliability). Source file: src/pipeline.py, lines 48-70 (__init__) and 155-170 (run entry). Currently the pipeline starts running stages without validating that config paths are valid, embedding providers are available, or required directories exist. Stages discover these issues mid-execution, producing confusing errors. Adding upfront validation follows the fail-fast principle.

userStories.title: Enrich pipeline error messages with recovery suggestions and state context
acceptanceCriteria: When a stage fails, the error log includes current state summary (segment count, video count, match count)
When validate_inputs fails, the error message includes which CLI flag or checkpoint reset would fix it (e.g., '--fresh', '--match-only')
Pipeline.run() at src/pipeline.py:254-258 augments result.error with state context before logging
At least 3 common failure scenarios produce actionable recovery suggestions in their error output
Tests verify that error messages contain recovery hints for known failure patterns
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (developer experience). Source file: src/pipeline.py:213-258 (validation and error handling block). Currently line 255 logs 'Stage {name} failed: {error}' with no context about what state the pipeline was in or how to recover. The validate_inputs failure at line 216 also gives no hint about which flag to use. This change adds structured error context without changing control flow.

userStories.title: Persist failed stage metrics in pipeline instead of only successful ones
acceptanceCriteria: When a stage fails, its metrics (duration, items processed before failure) are still stored in self.stage_metrics
StageMetrics dataclass has a new 'failed' boolean field (default False) to distinguish failed from successful metrics
Pipeline.run() stores metrics for failed stages with failed=True before returning False
The final pipeline summary (if any) includes failed stage metrics alongside successful ones
Tests verify that after a stage failure, stage_metrics[failed_stage] exists and has failed=True
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (observability). Source files: src/pipeline.py:237-244 (metrics storage), src/stages/__init__.py (StageMetrics dataclass). Currently at pipeline.py:254 when a stage fails, the code returns False without storing any metrics. The elapsed time is computed at line 233 but only stored for successful stages. This makes post-mortem debugging harder since we lose how long the failed stage ran and how much work it completed.

userStories.title: Add checkpoint data schema validation to prevent silent corruption
acceptanceCriteria: CheckpointData.from_dict() validates that stage data dicts contain expected keys (at minimum, non-empty for stages before last_completed_stage)
A new validate() method on CheckpointData checks internal consistency: all stages before last_completed_stage have non-empty data
CheckpointManager.load() calls validate() after from_dict() and logs warnings for any inconsistencies found
CheckpointManager.save() validates that the stage_key maps to an actual field on CheckpointData before writing
Tests verify that loading a checkpoint with missing intermediate stage data produces a warning
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (reliability). Source file: src/checkpoint.py:62-85 (CheckpointData), 150-194 (load), 440+ (save). Currently CheckpointData.from_dict() at line 84 filters to known fields but doesn't validate contents. The save() method uses stage.lower() to find the field name but has no guard against unknown stage names. If someone adds a stage without adding a field to CheckpointData, save() silently drops data.

userStories.title: Extract duplicated video ID extraction logic into a shared utility
acceptanceCriteria: A new function extract_video_id(path_or_id: str) -> Optional[str] exists in src/utils.py (or appropriate shared module)
The function uses the YouTube 11-character regex pattern r'([a-zA-Z0-9_-]{11})' with proper validation
src/stages/iterative_match.py replaces its inline _extract_video_id() and _extract_video_id_from_path() with the shared utility
src/state.py from_legacy_pipeline() (line 287) uses the shared utility instead of inline regex
All existing tests still pass after the refactor
userStories.notes: Tier: T3 (code quality). Source files: src/stages/iterative_match.py (two methods: _extract_video_id around line 652-674, _extract_video_id_from_path around line 1318-1322), src/state.py:287 (inline regex in from_legacy_pipeline). All three locations use the same regex pattern r'([a-zA-Z0-9_-]{11})' for YouTube ID extraction. Consolidating prevents drift between implementations.

userStories.title: Add cross-stage data flow integration tests for the full pipeline sequence
acceptanceCriteria: A new test file tests/integration/test_stage_transitions.py exists
Test verifies ANALYZE output (keywords, voiceover_segments) is valid input for VIDEO_SEARCH
Test verifies VIDEO_SEARCH output (video_ids, video_search_results) is valid input for CAPTION
Test verifies CAPTION output (text_metadata, caption_results) is valid input for MATCH
Test verifies MATCH output (matches, alternatives) is valid input for ITERATIVE_MATCH
All tests use mock data and do not require network access or API keys
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (test coverage). While individual stage tests are thorough (362 caption tests, 158 match tests, etc.), there are no tests verifying that one stage's output format is compatible with the next stage's expected input. This is how the stale PipelineState reference bug (state.embeddings) went undetected. Each test should create minimal mock output from stage N and pass it through stage N+1's validate_inputs() and initial state checks.

userStories.title: Harmonize match serialization and deserialization validation between MATCH and ITERATIVE_MATCH stages
acceptanceCriteria: ITERATIVE_MATCH restore (src/stages/iterative_match.py) applies the same confidence clamping [0,1] as MATCH restore (src/stages/match.py:284-286)
ITERATIVE_MATCH restore validates video_file is not empty string, matching MATCH stage behavior
A shared helper function (or base class method) handles match dict-to-object conversion used by both stages
Tests verify that both stages produce identical Match objects from the same checkpoint dict input
Tests verify that out-of-range confidence values (negative, >1) are clamped consistently
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (consistency). Source files: src/stages/match.py:246-314 (MATCH restore with extensive validation including confidence clamping), src/stages/iterative_match.py:496-519 (ITERATIVE_MATCH restore with minimal validation). The asymmetry means invalid data that MATCH would catch and fix can slip through ITERATIVE_MATCH restore unchecked. The confidence clamping is at match.py:284-286; iterative_match.py has no equivalent.

userStories.title: Add video count consistency assertion between video_ids, caption_results, and text_metadata
acceptanceCriteria: MATCH stage validate_inputs() checks that len(state.caption_results) > 0 when text_metadata is populated
A warning is logged if len(state.video_ids) differs from len(state.caption_results) by more than 10%
The consistency check accounts for expected drops (failed captions, filtered videos) and only warns, does not fail
Tests verify the warning triggers when video_ids has 100 entries but caption_results only has 50
Tests verify no warning when counts differ by less than 10%
userStories.notes: Tier: T3 (defensive). Source files: src/stages/match.py:326+ (validate_inputs), src/state.py:148-155 (the three fields). Currently there are three independent sources of truth for video counts: state.video_ids (from VIDEO_SEARCH), state.caption_results (from CAPTION, keyed by video_id), and state.text_metadata (populated from caption_results). No assertion checks that these are consistent, so silent data loss between stages goes undetected.

userStories.title: Add checkpoint backup timestamp comparison before restore
acceptanceCriteria: CheckpointManager.load() compares timestamps of main checkpoint and backup before selecting which to restore
If backup is newer than main (indicating a mid-save crash), a warning is logged explaining the situation
If main checkpoint is corrupt, load falls back to backup with a clear log message including both timestamps
Tests verify that when main checkpoint has an older timestamp than backup, the backup is preferred
Tests verify that when main is valid and newer, main is used even if backup also exists
userStories.notes: Tier: T3 (robustness). Source file: src/checkpoint.py:152-194 (load method). Currently at line 173-175, if the main checkpoint fails to load, the backup is restored without comparing timestamps. This means if the backup is actually older/staler than the (slightly corrupt) main, we may lose more progress than necessary. The timestamps are already present in CheckpointData fields created_at and updated_at (lines 65-66).

userStories.title: Add _STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS entries for missing state fields to prevent None fallbacks
acceptanceCriteria: _STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS in src/stages/__init__.py includes 'video_ids': [] entry
_STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS includes 'video_search_results': [] entry
_STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS includes 'downloaded_segments': [] entry
_STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS includes 'output_files': [] entry
All entries in _STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS match the default_factory types defined in PipelineState (src/state.py:131-171)
Tests verify that validate_required_state_attrs initializes missing fields to the correct type (list, dict) not None
userStories.notes: Tier: T2 (defensive). Source file: src/stages/__init__.py:249-260 (_STATE_ATTR_DEFAULTS dict). Currently the defaults dict has entries for text_metadata, caption_results, voiceover_segments, matches, embeddings, videos, keywords, alternatives, location_chapters. Missing: video_ids, video_search_results, downloaded_segments, output_files, otio_files, search_failed_keywords, face_preference, topic_context, extracted_entities. When validate_required_state_attrs encounters a missing attr not in this dict, it falls back to None (line 288), which can cause downstream TypeError when code expects a list.
